source.label: Turan's weak Lindelof hypothesis and its density theorem

reviewer: Claude Code reading of a published source; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: Published (Turan 1984, Section 37, Theorem 37.1). Weak Lindelof hypothesis with constant A: there is delta < A such that zeta has fewer than A delta log tau0 zeros in the disk of radius delta about s0 = sigma0 + i tau0 whenever zeta has no zero in Re s > sigma0, |Im s - tau0| < log tau0, sigma0 >= 1/2 + 10 delta, tau0 large. If it holds with some A < 0.01 then N(alpha, T) < T^(2(1 - alpha) + 5 sqrt A) for 1/2 <= alpha <= 1 and T large.
claims.assessment: Statement read as page images from a supplied scan; the proof read only in its first two pages; not audited. The book adds, citing an earlier paper of its author, that the count holds unconditionally with A = 0.71 (a constant read from a small scan and uncertain) for all delta < 1/10, and with every A at sigma0 = 1.
claims.rationale: A local count of zeros at the edge of a zero-free rectangle, weaker than the Lindelof hypothesis, which is the kind of count the notebook's shell exclusion needs when the excluded zero is the rightmost in a window.
claims.next_action: Read the cited source for the unconditional constant and compare with the shell exclusion's requirement.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.
